interface.name: deck_localization_v1
interface.description: What every system overlay needs to render its copy: the device language. One global, bound by the overlay framework for every overlay, so no per-feature protocol has to carry it. An overlay can ask for a language too, so the device switches it without a browser. A compositor of a device that does not offer its languages advertises no such global.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Release the binding. No further events are sent.

event.name: language
event.description: The language of every user-facing text, as the BCP-47 tag the device setting carries ("en-GB", "zh"). A string rather than an enum: the languages are the packs the device loads, which no list could name. Null when the device no longer offers the language its setting carries: it then speaks English and no offered language is current. An overlay falls back to English on a tag it does not know. Sent on bind and whenever the language changes.

request.name: set_language

description.summary: make the device speak a language

request.description: Ask the compositor to persist `value` as the device language: one of the tags the device offers, exactly as it offers it. The answer is a `language` event to every binding, this one included: the new language once it is saved, or the language in effect when the request changes nothing, being a tag the device does not offer or the one it already speaks.

event.name: languages
event.description: Every language `set_language` accepts, as BCP-47 tags separated by single spaces, the device's own order kept: the list a language picker shows. Sent on bind and whenever the list changes, always before `language`.
